history: Started as the Tri-Cities Blackhawks, then played in Milwaukee and St. Louis, where they won the 1958 title. In Atlanta since 1968.
One of the original teams from 1946 and the most successful franchise in the league, with 18 titles. Won 8 in a row from 1959 to 1966 with Bill Russell.
Began in the ABA as the New Jersey Americans and won two ABA titles with Julius Erving. Joined the NBA in 1976 and moved from New Jersey to Brooklyn in 2012.
Joined in 1988 as the Hornets. That team moved to New Orleans in 2002, the Charlotte Bobcats started in 2004 and took back the Hornets name in 2014.
Joined in 1966. Michael Jordan and Scottie Pippen led them to six titles in eight years in the 1990s, including the 72-10 season in 1995-96.
Joined in 1970. Their only title came in 2016, when LeBron James and Kyrie Irving came back from 3-1 down against Golden State.
Joined in 1980. Dirk Nowitzki played all 21 seasons in Dallas and won the 2011 title and Finals MVP against Miami.
Began in the ABA and joined the NBA in 1976. Nikola Jokić, a second-round pick, led them to their first title in 2023.
Started as the Fort Wayne Pistons and moved to Detroit in 1957. The tough 'Bad Boys' won two titles in 1989 and 1990, and a team without a superstar won again in 2004.
An original team from 1946 as the Philadelphia Warriors. Moved to San Francisco in 1962. Stephen Curry changed the game with the three-pointer and won four titles.
Started as the San Diego Rockets in 1967 and moved to Houston in 1971. Hakeem Olajuwon won back-to-back titles in 1994 and 1995.
Won three ABA titles before joining the NBA in 1976. Reached the NBA Finals in 2000 and 2025 but are still waiting for an NBA title.
Started as the Buffalo Braves in 1970, became the San Diego Clippers in 1978 and moved to Los Angeles in 1984. Opened their own arena, the Intuit Dome, in 2024.
Started as the Minneapolis Lakers, where they won five titles, and moved to Los Angeles in 1960. With 17 titles they are second only to Boston.
Joined in 1995 as the Vancouver Grizzlies and moved to Memphis in 2001. Known for the tough 'Grit and Grind' teams of the 2010s.
Joined in 1988. Dwyane Wade won the 2006 title, then LeBron James, Wade and Chris Bosh won two more in 2012 and 2013.
Joined in 1968 and won the title in only their third season with a young Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. Giannis Antetokounmpo brought the second title in 2021.
Joined in 1989. Kevin Garnett won the MVP award here in 2004. Anthony Edwards led them to the Western Conference Finals in 2024 and 2025.
The Charlotte Hornets moved here in 2002 and became the Pelicans in 2013. Anthony Davis, the first pick of the 2012 draft, was their biggest star for seven seasons.
An original team from 1946 that plays in the oldest arena in the league. Won in 1970 and 1973, then had to wait 53 years until Jalen Brunson led them to the 2026 title.
Started as the Seattle SuperSonics in 1967 and won the 1979 title there. Moved to Oklahoma City in 2008 and won again in 2025 with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.
Joined in 1989. Reached the Finals twice, with Shaquille O'Neal in 1995 and with Dwight Howard in 2009.
Started as the Syracuse Nationals and won the 1955 title there. Moved to Philadelphia in 1963 and won with Wilt Chamberlain in 1967 and with Julius Erving and Moses Malone in 1983.
Joined in 1968. Reached the Finals three times (1976, 1993 and 2021). Steve Nash won two MVP awards here with a fast 'seven seconds or less' offense.
Joined in 1970 and won the 1977 title with Bill Walton. Damian Lillard became famous here for his game-winning shots from very far away.
Started as the Rochester Royals and won the 1951 title. Played in Cincinnati and Kansas City before moving to Sacramento in 1985.
Began in the ABA and joined the NBA in 1976. Tim Duncan and coach Gregg Popovich won five titles. Victor Wembanyama led them back to the Finals in 2026.
Joined in 1995 and is the only team outside the United States. Won the 2019 title with Kawhi Leonard and Kyle Lowry.
Started as the New Orleans Jazz in 1974 and moved to Utah in 1979. John Stockton and Karl Malone reached the Finals in 1997 and 1998 but lost both to Chicago.
Started as the Chicago Packers in 1961, then became the Baltimore Bullets and moved to Washington in 1973. Won the 1978 title and became the Wizards in 1997.
